title: How Much Fiber in Butternut Squash? 6.6g per Cup
description: Butternut Squash: about 6.6 g of fiber per 1 cup cubes, baked (23% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in butternut squash?

answer.detail: fiber in 1 cup cubes, baked (205 g)
answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Squash, winter, butternut, cooked, baked, without salt

intro: Butternut squash ranks #2 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in butternut squash by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in butternut squash?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists squash, winter, butternut, cooked, baked, without salt at 3.2 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup cubes, baked; 205 g) therefore has about 6.6 g of fiber and 82 calories. That is 23% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 26% of a 25 g day and 17% of a 38 g day.

Baked butternut squash is one of the better fiber sources among sweet, starchy vegetables, with more fiber per cooked cup than sweet potato flesh. It is a fall and winter staple for soups and roasting.

sections.heading: Roasted cubes vs squash soup
paragraphs: Roasting concentrates squash, so a cup of roasted cubes is denser than a cup of raw cubes.
Butternut soup is often thinned with stock and cream. A cup of soup can have well under half the squash of a cup of roasted cubes.

sections.heading: How butternut squash compares with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, butternut squash ranks #2 for fiber per typical serving and #6 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 8 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [artichoke](/fiber-in-artichoke) at 6.9 g (1 medium globe artichoke, raw (edible part)); [broccoli](/fiber-in-broccoli) at 5.1 g (1 cup chopped, cooked); [kale](/fiber-in-kale) at 4.7 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), butternut squash is #9 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding butternut squash to your day
paragraphs: Roast cubes and add to grain bowls with chickpeas, or blend into a thick soup with white beans to raise the fiber.

Example: 1 cup butternut squash, 1/2 cup chickpeas, 1 cup quinoa. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 18 g of fiber, with 6.6 g from the butternut squash. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of butternut squash?
faqs.a: 3.2 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Squash, winter, butternut, cooked, baked, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in butternut squash (1/2 cup cubes, baked)?
faqs.a: About 3.3 g, for 102.5 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Is butternut squash high in fiber?
faqs.a: Baked, a cup is about a quarter of the Daily Value, which is high for a vegetable.
Plain canned pumpkin is also a good source, about 7 g per cup in USDA data. Pumpkin pie filling has added sugar.
